two/prompt: A denoiser can take a text prompt as an extra input, such as a red bicycle, and guess the noise with it in mind. Call that guess epsilon c: c for conditioned, shown the prompt.
two/drop: Train it with the prompt replaced by an empty one part of the time. Then the same network can also guess without the prompt: epsilon u, u for unconditioned.
two/diff: The difference, epsilon c minus epsilon u, is what the prompt changes: the direction the prompt points.
push/rule: Guidance mixes the two. The guess it uses, epsilon hat, is epsilon u, plus w times the difference. Here w is not a weight but one number, the guidance scale.
push/ends: At w equal to zero, that is just epsilon u: the prompt is ignored. At w equal to one, it is exactly epsilon c.
push/three: Above one, it steps past epsilon c, further the way the prompt points. At w equal to three: zero point two plus three times zero point three is one point one, and minus zero point four plus zero point nine is zero point five.
push/use: An image is made by taking the guessed noise away a little at a time, over many steps. Guidance swaps in this guess at every step, so each step runs the network twice: once with the prompt, once without.
scale/sweep: So what does a larger w buy? Every step leans harder toward what the prompt asks for.
scale/low: At w of one, the pictures vary a lot, and some follow the prompt only loosely.
scale/mid: Around seven, they follow it closely. Values like this are a common default.
scale/big: Push w much higher, and the pictures look more and more alike, with colors and contrast overdone. Guidance trades variety for faithfulness to the prompt.
